item.title: The U.S. last held a public execution in the 1930s. The Pentagon wants to change that
item.description: The Pentagon says it will livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan at Fort Hood, the site of his 2009 mass shooting. That would be the first public execution in the U.S. since the 1930s.
item.content:encoded:
The Pentagon says it will livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan at Fort Hood, the site of his 2009 mass shooting. That would be the first public execution in the U.S. since the 1930s.

(Image credit: Getty Images)

item.title: U.S. working to reverse an Egyptian man's third-country deportation to Africa
item.description: The Trump administration's effort to return Ahmed Soliman to the U.S. come after an Arizona judge said his deportation violated due process.

item.title: Did Russia play by the rules in reporting lab worker's death?
item.description: A global treaty signed by 197 countries — including Russia — requires reporting any death that could be a sign of an outbreak to come.

item.title: Five children are taken from their parents in 'Fjord,' which won top prize at Cannes
item.description: Cristian Mungiu's latest film takes place in a small Norwegian town, where a recently arrived couple stands accused of abusing their children — but in Fjord, the truth is never quite clear.

item.title: 'Misty Green' squanders its potential
item.description: Chris Rock's new movie Misty Green wants to critique Hollywood's treatment of Black women. Instead, it gives star Rosalind Eleazar a half-baked role while Rock plays a moralizing savior we've seen before.

item.title: ChatGPT for Teens has special safeguards. A watchdog group finds most don't work
item.description: A study from Common Sense Media says most safeguards in ChatGPT for Teens failed. The chatbot talks to teens like a friend and doesn't alert parents when users talk about self-harm and suicide.
